This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter to activate.

Accessible Form

Fields marked * are required.

For example, name@example.com
Up to 2,000 characters.

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

Interactive Counter

This counter demonstrates state management and ARIA live regions for accessible dynamic content.

content.text:
I made six targeted fixes to `0.html`, but none of them have been tested in a browser or with a screen reader. The shell command I tried to run was blocked because this session can't approve it, so the contrast figures below are hand-calculated.

## What changed

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Card hover ignored reduced-motion.** The `.card` transition and lift on hover sat outside the `prefers-reduced-motion` block, unlike every other animation on the page. | Moved the transition into the motion block and gated the lift on `no-preference`. The shadow change on hover still applies for everyone. |
| **Counter announced twice.** `<output>` is a live region by default, so each click announced both the bare number and "Count is now N." | Added `aria-live="off"` to the `<output>`, leaving the descriptive message as the only announcement. |
| **Form success message might not be announced.** `#form-status` was `display: none` until filled, and some screen readers miss live regions that are hidden at the moment they get content. | The element now stays rendered and takes up no space when empty; its box styling applies only when it has text. |
| **Error message had the same problem.** `.error-message` was also `display: none` when empty. | Same treatment: it stays rendered, with the margin applied only when it has text. |
| **Success text fell short of AA.** `#2e7d32` on the tinted status background comes to about 4.3:1, below the 4.5:1 the page claims. | Darkened the light-mode `--success` to `#1b5e20`, about 6.6:1. Dark mode was already fine at about 6:1. |
| **Inline styles in the counter.** | Moved to a `.counter` class, which also adds wrapping on narrow screens, tabular numerals so the digits don't shift, and a logical margin on the Reset button. |

I also removed the unused `--accent-light` variable from both themes.

## Left alone

- **Content security policy:** it still allows inline scripts and styles. With the inline style attributes gone you could switch to hashes, but they break on every edit to the file, so I left it.
- **Author meta tag:** it holds your email address in plain text, which scrapers can harvest if this page is published. Swap it for a name if that matters to you.
